content_preview.title: Kotlin 2.4.20 Ships With Sealed-Class Swift Export, New Wasm Compilation Modes and an Experimental Native Compiler Image
content_preview.summary: Kotlin 2.4.20, released September 7, maps sealed classes to Swift enums, adds new Kotlin/Wasm compilation modes, and ships a first experimental native compiler image.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

JetBrains released Kotlin 2.4.20 on [September 7](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/whatsnew2420.html), a minor update that touches the standard library, Kotlin/Native, Kotlin/Wasm, Kotlin/JS, Gradle tooling, the Build Tools API and the compiler itself. According to the [official "What's new in Kotlin 2.4.20" page](https://kotlinlang.org/docs/whatsnew2420.html), the release's headline changes include new Swift export capabilities for sealed classes, additional Kotlin/Wasm compilation mode...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece covering the Kotlin 2.4.20 point release across Swift export, Kotlin/Wasm, standard library, Kotlin/JS, and tooling changes. Section headers organize distinct feature areas clearly, and the 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags the absence of adoption figures and benchmark methodology.
editor_notes.source_verification: Both sources decompressed and read in full from local snapshots (not re-fetched): source-0.html.gz (kotlinlang.org/docs/whatsnew2420.html, sha256 c6495c4c... verified against manifest) and source-1.html.gz (blog.jetbrains.com JetBrains announcement, sha256 ad69975b... verified against manifest). Both fetched with HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no suspicious_patterns flagged in either manifest entry. Verified against source-0: the 'Released: September 7, 2026' line (exact match, confirming the article correctly used the kotlinlang.org date rather than any GitHub-derived date); the sealed-class-to-Swift-enum quote and 'reverse import' language; the assembleSharedXCFramework/Package.swift claim; all three Wasm compilation mode names (monolith, multimodule-open-world, multimodule-closed-world); the 5-10% Wasm binary-size reduction figure tied to the KotlinConf application; the wasmWasi/Wasmtime claim; the StackTraceRecoverable interface and its verbatim quoted rationale; all four allDistinct/allDistinctBy/allEqual/allEqualBy function names; the kotlin.test/JUnit 5 alignment quote; the Playwright/Mocha DSL and 'deprecated for two years' quote on Karma; the Build Tools API opt-in properties and the 'Starting with Kotlin 2.5.0' default-enablement date; the kotlinr rename and naming-conflict rationale with Kotlin Toolchain; the native-image 'drop-in replacement' verbatim quote; the Gradle 9.7.0/Problems API diagnostic-ID claim; and the klib incremental-compilation Beta status originating in Kotlin 1.9.20. Verified against source-1: the opening 'The Kotlin 2.4.20 release is out! Here are the main highlights:' quote is verbatim.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: All specifics traced to source-0 confirmed accurate and correctly attributed. One subordinate inaccuracy found: the article's closing section states the JetBrains blog 'summarizes the release in six bullet points spanning the standard library, Kotlin/Native, Kotlin/Wasm, Kotlin/JS, Gradle and the Build Tools API.' Source-1 actually lists seven bullet categories (Standard library, Kotlin/Native, Kotlin/Wasm, Kotlin/JS, Gradle, Build tools API, and Kotlin compiler) — the article's count is off by one and omits 'Kotlin compiler' from the enumerated list. This is a minor, isolated miscount of the source's own structure, not a claim about Kotlin 2.4.20 itself, and does not affect the headline, summary, or lead. No other discrepancies found; no fabricated or hallucinated specifics identified.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional throughout, consistent with News category conventions. No editorializing or sensationalism.
editor_notes.originality: Checked against prior published coverage. Distinct from three prior Kotlin/JetBrains articles in the archive: src/content/articles/2026-04/22-kotlin-2320-... (Kotlin 2.3.20, April — destructuring, Gradle 9.3, Wasm perf), src/content/articles/2026-06/08-kotlin-240-... (Kotlin 2.4.0, June — context parameters, K1 retirement), and src/content/articles/2026-09/02-compose-multiplatform-112-... (Compose Multiplatform 1.12, Sept 2 — a separate JetBrains UI framework product, covering an MCP server for AI agents). This submission covers Kotlin 2.4.20 (Sept 7), a later point release with an entirely different feature set (Swift sealed-class export, Wasm compilation modes, native compiler image). No re-narration of prior archive content found; this is genuinely new coverage.
concerns: The article states the JetBrains blog post summarizes the release in 'six bullet points' when the source actually lists seven categories (the article omits 'Kotlin compiler' from its enumeration). This is a subordinate, non-lead claim describing the source's presentation structure rather than a fact about Kotlin 2.4.20 itself.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced submission with accurate technical claims throughout and confirmed originality against prior Kotlin/Compose Multiplatform coverage. One isolated, minor miscount in a subordinate sentence (six vs. seven bullet points in the source's summary) is recoverable with a public corrections note; everything else — including the September 7, 2026 release date the contributor bot flagged as deliberately sourced from kotlinlang.org — is verified accurate. APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS.
